key_insight: SJ-KAN propagates spatial derivatives analytically through a compact spectral network, achieving comparable or better accuracy than PINN and PIKAN baselines with up to 47× fewer parameters and 8.2× faster training per epoch.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce training cost for physics-informed incompressible flow solvers, including high-Reynolds-number lid-driven cavity simulations.
method: Embed coordinates in Chebyshev bases and precompute their derivatives at collocation points.
Compress the bases into a few latent features, then predict physical variables with one nonlinear Chebyshev KAN layer.
Evaluate Navier–Stokes spatial derivatives analytically; use automatic differentiation only for weight-gradient backpropagation.
evidence_signal: Three SJ-KAN variants were compared with PINN and PIKAN on Taylor–Green vortex and lid-driven cavity benchmarks, with cavity tests reaching Re = 10,000 without reference data and using fewer than 9,000 trainable parameters.
watch_item: Evaluation is limited to the reported benchmarks; performance on complex geometries and broader flow regimes remains unestablished.
paper_title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
